newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Next IMF tranche to ex-Soviet Georgia seen soon.
newsitem.headline: Next IMF tranche to ex-Soviet Georgia seen soon.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Georgia will soon receive the first tranche of the $80 million of an International Monetary Fund which is due to be paid in 1997, representative Hunter Monroe said on Monday.
He told reporters the $40 million tranche of the 1997 loan package would be transfered to the National Bank's account in the next few days and would be used to provide backing for the lari currency.
Another $40 million could be allocated to the republic in September or October, after an IMF mission visits to Georgia at the end of July.

"The improvement of the main macroeconomic indicators convinced us of the necessity of cooperation with Georgia," he said. "The Georgian parliament adopted a realistic budget, which is not aimed at printing money."
Monroe said the adoption of the budget was the single most important factor in the IMF's decision to continue its lending programme.

But he also highlighted a fall in annual inflation to 14 percent in 1996 from 50,000 percent in 1993, the stable lari and the signing of debt-rescheduling deals between Georgia and several creditor states.

Weak points included low tax revenues and problems in the energy sector. "In spite of the increasing of tax revenues to eight percent of GDP (Gross Domestic Product) in 1996, (from two percent in 1994) this level remains very low," he said.
The 1997 loan is part of a three-year $246 million package, $80 million of which was disbursed in 1996.
